title: Flow Atlas model definitions
description: Shared definitions. Every document has apiVersion and kind, after the Kubernetes Resource Model, and a provenance after SLSA: the tool, its parameters and every input it read with a digest. Nothing in a document depends on when or where it was written.

surfaceId.description: component|METHOD /path, the path as an OpenAPI path template: parameters are written {name}, never :name.

callId.description: from->to|METHOD /path@file#scope, or @file:line without a scope; ~n tells repeats apart

chainId.description: <entry>-><surface id>: the component that makes the request, or outside for a surface declared public, and the surface that serves it.

evidence.description: declared: a manifest states it. static: parsed syntax. text: matched as text. name: joined because a method name agrees.

operationId.description: The OpenAPI operationId, when the code states it, the configured convention gives it, or a document declares it.

described.description: Where the component's OpenAPI document declares this operation.

describedPath.description: The path key that document writes the operation under, which may differ from `path` by a base path, a trailing slash or parameter names.

describedVersion.description: That document's version: 2.0 for Swagger, otherwise its openapi value.

reaches.description: Member methods the handler calls, following local and relatively imported functions. Absent when the handler was not read.

implicit.description: Served by the framework with no handler written for it, as Next.js answers HEAD with GET's handler and OPTIONS with an Allow header and serves the files of public/, FastAPI its OpenAPI document and Spring Boot its error page; requested by convention from outside the code, as crawlers fetch Next.js's robots.txt and sitemaps; or by the framework's own client, as a Next.js Server Action posts to its page. No rule expects a caller for it.

convention.description: The rule of the framework that serves the route where no code of the application handles it, with at the place that brings it in: fastapi docs_url, spring-boot error, next public, @fastify/static.

patterns.description: The regular expression the text of each parameter named here must match, as its router tests it: Fastify's :file(^\d+) and Hono's :date{[0-9]+}, and where a parameter shares its segment, Fastify's (.*?) and Spring's (.*). A parameter not named takes some text of its segment, or the whole segment.

dispatch.description: How the route's router picks it among the routes a request fits and treats a trailing /, as its framework documents it. A field left out is a rule atlas does not read for the route; matching then keeps every route a request fits, with or without a trailing /.

picks.description: registration: the first route registered that a request fits answers it (Express, @koa/router, Hono, Nest on Express, Starlette), by order. find-my-way: Fastify's router tries static text before a parameter, a parameter with a regexp before one without, and a parameter before a wildcard. specificity: Nest's routeResolutionStrategy 'specificity' registers the more specific routes first, by rank, and routes of one rank in order. werkzeug: Werkzeug's matcher (Flask, Quart) tries a segment's static text before its variables, and variables by their weight, whatever the order, by parts. precedence: ASP.NET Core's endpoint routing takes, of the routes whose template and constraints a request meets, the one first by rank (lower first), and of those a route that names the request's method before one that takes any (EndpointComparer, HttpMethodMatcherPolicy); routes left tied are ambiguous. httprouter: Gin's tree tries, segment by segment, static text before a parameter and a parameter before a catch-all, whatever the order. chi: chi's tree tries, from each place in the path, static text, then a parameter with a regexp, then one without, then a catch-all, whatever the order, a mounted router's routes as a catch-all at their mount (mounted). servemux: Go's ServeMux (1.22 and later) takes the most specific pattern: one with a method before one without, and segment by segment a literal before a wildcard before a remainder.

rank.description: For specificity, the kind of each segment of the route's path as Nest's specificity sort ranks it (RouteSpecificitySorter): a literal 0, text with a parameter 2, a parameter 3, a wildcard 4. For precedence, the route's Order (any integer) and then the digit of each segment of its template (RoutePrecedence.ComputeInbound): a literal 1, a constrained parameter or a segment of several parts 2, a parameter 3, a constrained catch-all 4, a catch-all 5. Which values each takes is checked by picks.

parts.description: The parts of the route's rule as Werkzeug's StateMachineMatcher holds them, one a segment from the first (a variable that takes slashes, path, makes one part of the rest), a / at the end left out (trailing says it): a static part's text, or a part with variables: its regular expression as Werkzeug compiles it (the same for two parts Werkzeug keeps in one state; a converter whose regex is not read stands as its class) and its weight (Weighting, flattened), which orders the parts tried at one position. No weight where a converter's is not read.

mounted.description: chi: the number of segments of the route's path before each router mounted on the way to the route's (Mount, Route), from the outermost; chi's tree matches a mount as a catch-all after its path, then the mounted router's tree.

order.description: Where the route is registered, from the router a request enters down to the one that holds it: each step a sequence of registrations whose order is known (router) and the place in it (at). Of two routes, the one before is the one whose steps first differ in at within the same router; routes whose steps first differ in router are in no order atlas knows.

passes.description: The handler takes the next it may pass the request on with, so a route registered after it may answer too.

byPath.description: The router picks a route by the request's path alone, and the route answers a method it does not take with 405 (Django: the first pattern the path fits, whatever the method), so a route after it that takes the method is not reached.

slashes.description: How the router treats a / at the end of a request's path: ignored (Express, @koa/router), strict (a path with it is another path: Fastify, Hono, Spring 6 and later), redirected (Starlette redirects a request no route takes to the path with the / added or removed where a route takes that), removed and added (Next.js redirects every request to the path without it, or with it, by trailingSlash), appended (Werkzeug serves the path as the route writes it, and redirects a request without the / to the path with it where a route written with one takes that, unless its matcher reaches a route that takes the request as written first: strict_slashes), append-slash (Django serves the path as the pattern writes it, and CommonMiddleware answers a request without the / that no pattern takes as written with a redirect to the path with it, where the first pattern that takes that is this route's: APPEND_SLASH), tsr (Gin serves the path as the route writes it, and redirects a request to the path with the / added or removed where the route its tree reaches first takes that form: RedirectTrailingSlash), subtree (Go's ServeMux serves the path as the pattern writes it, and redirects a request without a / that no pattern but a remainder or subtree matches to the path with it, where a pattern matches that with nothing left for its remainder).

trailing.description: The route's path as served ends with a / (slash), or is served with and without one (both). On a route that ends in a wildcard, slash says the path before the wildcard is served only with the /.

constrained.description: The router takes a request to the route only where its headers meet a constraint (Fastify's constraints), or may, where the route's options are not spelled out.

caseless.description: The router matches the literal text of the path whatever its case (ASP.NET Core).

unchecked.description: Parameters whose constraint atlas does not read as a regular expression (ASP.NET Core's min(2000), guid, one the application registers): the router may refuse a value the path takes there, so the route takes a request from no other route for certain.

call.description: A request one component makes to another, found at a call site.

path.description: Request path; {} marks an interpolated value.

based.description: The call site joins a base address to the path.

slash.description: The call site writes a / at the end of the path, which path leaves out.

scope.description: The function or method that holds the call site.

page.description: For a URL relative to the page that holds it (a page-relative link, a form with no action): the path of the routes whose page it was resolved against; only those routes reach the call.

edge.description: match: a call reaches a surface by method and path (call id to surface id). reach: a surface's handler calls the method via, which holds an outbound call (surface id to call id).

resourceDescriptor.description: An input a document was made from, after the in-toto ResourceDescriptor.

name.description: What the input is to this document: code, config, flows, or base/head variants.

uri.description: Repository-relative location; . for the repository itself.

digest.description: gitCommit for code read from a commit (a SHA-1 or SHA-256 object name), sha256 for files; absent for an uncommitted working tree.

provenance.description: How the document was produced. The four fields take their names and meaning from SLSA provenance v1, flattened: this is not an in-toto statement or a SLSA predicate (no _type, subject, buildDefinition or runDetails). Dependencies are in-toto ResourceDescriptors. No timestamps or machine paths.

condition.description: After Kubernetes status conditions, without lastTransitionTime so that the same inputs give the same document.

apiDocument.description: An OpenAPI description of a component. file: committed, location is the repository path. served: the component serves it, location is the path on the server; the origin depends on the environment.

aliasOf.description: A served path that shows another served document, as a swagger UI's uiConfig.url does.

agreement.description: For a committed file: how many of the component's routes it declares, which it lacks, and how many operations it adds.

apiDescription.description: Which description is a component's, decided only where the code decides it: the author's openapi entry, the one committed file that declares every route, else the one served document (aliases collapsed), else a single partial file. Otherwise ambiguous, with the candidates.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and an explicit UTC offset. The pattern bounds each field; the date-time format, which the validator asserts, checks the calendar day.

actor.description: Who wrote a source: <producer>/<version> for agents and tools, human:<id> for people, process:<id> for automated processes, as OKF 0.2 §7 writes actors.

okfSource.description: A material the flow derives from, shaped as an OKF 0.2 §5.1 source.

resource.description: Absolute URL, repository-relative path, or a scope descriptor.
